# Results — Study 60 (Long-Shot): the skewness (lottery) effect in commodities, 2009–2026

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Daily returns of a **14-commodity ETF
basket** (GLD, SLV, USO, UNG, DBA, DBB, CORN, WEAT, SOYB, PPLT, PALL, DBC, GSG, UGA), Yahoo. Signal =
trailing-12-month return skewness; long the low-skew third, short the high-skew. As-of 2026-06; inputs
fingerprint `de0a072075bb`.*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `WEAK` · Tradability `FRAGILE` · "Skewness/lottery effect is real"? `SUPPORTED`

The lottery story — investors overpay for positively-skewed, jackpot-like bets, so high-skew commodities
underperform — points the **right way** on the tape: the long-low/short-high-skew trade earns
**+5.2%/yr (hit 53%)** and is **stable** (Sharpe 0.28 then 0.27 across the two halves). But it's `WEAK`:
the Sharpe is **0.27 (Lo t 1.1)** — not significant — over only **14 commodities**, too thin a
cross-section to clinch it. And `FRAGILE`: commodity ETF costs and roll erode it (net Sharpe **0.19 at
10 bp**, 0.08 at 25 bp). The sign and the literature (Fuertes-Miffre-Fernandez 2015) say `SUPPORTED`; the
small universe just can't confirm the magnitude.

## Data stamp

- **Basket**: 14 commodity ETFs, daily, 2009–2026, 210 months, fingerprint `de0a072075bb`

## Low-skew commodities beat high-skew — modestly

| long low-skew / short high-skew | value |
|---|---|
| mean | **+5.2%/yr** |
| Sharpe | **0.27** |
| Lo t-stat | 1.1 |
| hit rate | 53% |

| | Sharpe |
|---|---|
| 2009–2017 | +0.28 |
| 2018–on | +0.27 |

The direction is right and remarkably stable across the sample — exactly what the behavioural story
predicts (avoid the over-bid lottery commodities). But a t of 1.1 over a 14-name basket is suggestive,
not conclusive.

## …and costs thin it further

| cost / trade | net Sharpe |
|---|---|
| gross | 0.27 |
| 10 bp | **0.19** |
| 25 bp | 0.08 |

Commodity ETFs carry roll yield drag and wider spreads than equities, so realistic costs pull an already
modest Sharpe toward zero. The signal survives at low cost but has little cushion.

## Why it's `WEAK`, not confirmed

1. **Tiny cross-section.** 14 ETFs (a low-skew and high-skew third of ~5 names each) is far fewer than
   the futures universes the literature uses; the t-stat is starved of breadth.
2. **ETF frictions.** Roll yield ([Study 35 Contango](../../35-contango/)) and spreads erode commodity
   long-shorts more than equity ones.
3. **But the sign holds, persistently.** Unlike the inverted equity lottery studies
   ([53 Jackpot](../../53-jackpot/) / [54 Static](../../54-static/)), the commodity skewness effect points
   the *right* way and doesn't decay — consistent with a real behavioural premium.

## The honest takeaway

The commodity skewness/lottery effect is `WEAK` but `SUPPORTED`: long low-skew commodities beat high-skew
by ~5%/yr, the right sign, stable across the sample — yet a Sharpe of 0.27 (t 1.1) over just 14 ETFs,
thinned further by costs, can't confirm it. A real behavioural tilt seen through a small window — and, of
the recent bench, one of the few that at least leans the right way. `FRAGILE` to trade as is.
